must_remember: In a myopic eye, parallel rays from infinity form a real image in front of the retina due to excessive converging power or elongation of the eyeball.
The far point ($x$) of a myopic eye is at a finite distance in front of the eye, unlike the normal eye where it is at infinity.
Myopia is corrected using a diverging lens (concave lens) whose focal length magnitude equals the distance of the far point ($f = -x$).
The optical power of the corrective lens for myopia is always negative, expressed in diopters ($P = -1/x$).
A myopic person can see nearby objects clearly, but distant objects appear blurred because their far point is limited.

glossary.meaning: A defect of vision where distant objects are not seen clearly because images are formed in front of the retina.
The maximum distance up to which a myopic eye can clearly see objects without optical correction.
A diverging lens used as a corrective optical element for short-sightedness to diverge incoming rays.
The degree of convergence or divergence of a lens, measured in diopters ($D$), given by $P = 1/f$.
The transparent gelatinous tissue filling the eyeball behind the lens, where the premature image forms in myopia.
